subject: Split-routing token crediting and minimums for mixed-model sessions

Subject: Billing for split-routing / mixed-model sessions — need worked examples

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightCart is excited about Redwood's routing controls. Before we move further on the POC, procurement asked for a short write-up on how billing will behave for our main pattern: many customer-facing sessions start on the small low-cost variant (fast, cheap) and then selectively escalate to the higher-capacity model for specific generations (longer responses, tool use).

Key asks:
- When a single user session routes between two model variants, are tokens billed to each model separately (i.e., charge by model that actually generated the tokens)?
- Do we get any credit when KV/prefixes are reused across variants in the same session?
- How do rounding and minimums apply when a session produces small bursts to the expensive variant (e.g., 12 output tokens on the expensive model) but 98% of traffic stays on the cheap model?

I've attached a small sample of our call traces (BrightCart_usage_sample.csv) with counts by session-id to help illustrate. Procurement would like a sample invoice line or two showing how a blended invoice might look under your current rules.

Can you provide a short example and confirm whether there are discount/packaging levers we should ask for in contract (blended-rate, commit bands, or per-variant minimums)?

Appreciate it —
Holly

holly@brightcart.com

From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Billing for split-routing / mixed-model sessions — need worked examples

Hi Holly — thanks for the sample data. Short answers up front, then a worked example.

Summary (policy TL;DR):
1) Per-token attribution: billing is attributed to the model variant that actually served/generatd the token. Inputs + outputs are both counted; we bill the sum of tokens processed by each model.
2) KV/prefix reuse: if a request omits a prefix because it's satisfied by an active KV cache entry that Redwood serves from cache (zero-request payload), we do not bill those tokens again. However, cached prefix reuse credit is only applied when the cache hit is satisfied without rehydrating from an external call and when the serving variant is compatible with the cached representation.
3) Rounding & minimums: we round usage on invoice lines to our billing quantum (1 token for per-token SKUs, and to the nearest 1k token bucket when the customer is on a 1k quantum bundle). Small bursts are still billed to the expensive variant unless you have a blended concession. If you exceed your commit bands we apply standard overage pricing; below band usage is charged at committed rates with minimums enforced per billing period or per SKU depending on the contract.

Worked example (from your sample):
- Session A: 95 input tokens routed to cheap-x-small (model A) + 12 output tokens generated by expensive-x (model B) after escalation.
Billing:
  - model A: 95 tokens billed at model A rate (input tokens count)
  - model B: 12 tokens billed at model B rate (output tokens count)
Invoice lines:
  - Cheap variant (model A) — 95 tokens @ $0.0002 = $0.019
  - Expensive variant (model B) — 12 tokens @ $0.0035 = $0.042
  - Total for session A = $0.061 (rounded per quantum; no cross-model credit applied by default)

Note on KV/prefix credit: if the 95-token input was entirely a cached prefix (client-side omitted the text and Redwood served it from session cache), those 95 tokens would not appear on the invoice. But if the client supplies the 95 tokens in the request payload (even if identical to what was seen previously), they are billable unless a cache hit happened server-side.

Discount and packaging levers we can offer:
- Blended routing concession: for customers with >$X/month commit, we can offer an effective blended per-token rate for traffic that does N% routing to expensive variants. This is contractual and requires an agreed traffic steering baseline.
- Commit bands by class: you can commit total tokens across model families and we apply a blended discount across families rather than per-variant minimums.
- Burst protection: add a small reserved burst pool (flat monthly fee) that consumes expensive-variant bursts up to Y tokens per month at a discounted marginal rate.

I'll attach a short CSV that maps your sample sessions into invoice-like lines so procurement can see the dollar math. If you want a formal term sheet we'll loop in Ben for concessions.

Next steps: confirm which concession you want us to model and whether we should produce a draft term sheet for procurement.

Best,

Holly — great questions. Quick answers and I pasted a short invoice comparison below.

Caching across variants:
- Cache mechanics: Redwood's KV/prefix cache is keyed by (session-id, canonicalized prefix, model-family-compatibility). If model B is binary-compatible with the cached representation from model A (common in our aligned-family variants), model B can serve a cache hit without re-consuming tokens from storage. In that case, the server does not count the prefix tokens again because the tokens were never re-sent in the request payload.
- Practical rule: we bill what is actually processed in the request pipeline. If the client omits the prefix because Redwood served it from cache, no input tokens are counted. If the client resubmits the prefix in the request body (even identical), those bytes/tokens are billable.

Over-delivery under Option A (blended routing allowance):
- Month 1 spikes: the concession includes a soft burst buffer (5% of committed tokens) billed at the blended rate. Anything above the buffer is billed at the overage rate (standard expensive-family overage) unless we agree to a temporary top-up to your commit for that month. We can add a one-time promotional buffer if needed for launch weeks.

Sample invoice comparison (one heavy week):
Assumptions: 4M tokens in week; 92% on cheap family, 8% on expensive family; with Option A commit applied pro-rata to the week.
1) No concession:
  - Cheap-family: 3.68M tokens @ $0.0002 = $736.00
  - Expensive-family: 320k tokens @ $0.0035 = $1,120.00
  - Week total = $1,856.00
2) Option A blended concession (effective $0.0009/token for blended traffic up to commit):
  - All blended traffic up to committed baseline billed at $0.0009 (4M tokens * $0.0009 = $3,600) BUT because contract replaces per-variant pricing and includes committed guarantee the net effect depends on your committed minimums and whether the weekly consumption consumes committed tokens. This example shows the blended rate can be beneficial if your commit reduces per-token beyond overage bands — we'll model it precisely for annual commit vs observed usage.

Next steps:

- If you want, we can include a short clause in the term sheet to handle launch-week promotional buffers (one-off, non-recurring).
